execution_contract.host_writes: Shared COMMAND word only; CPU0 executes all lifecycle MMIO, CPU1 executes all CCOUNT/CCOMPARE instructions and interrupt handlers.
execution_contract.counter_observers: Guest RSR CCOUNT after release is mandatory alongside direct-index HMP CCOUNT. HMP-only equality of a lazy cached SR is insufficient. Preserve raw registers and INTSET, guest words, QMP, ROM/input hashes and serial output.
execution_contract.physical_clock_observer: Native CPU QOM clk-in-period directly reads the actual qdev clock. Missing old-image observation stays null and cannot pass; no inferred period or frequency fallback. Original clock tests still use qtest-clock-period under the qtest accelerator.
execution_contract.gate: CPU1 qdev input period is actually zero, CPU0 positive and unchanged. CCOUNT remains nonzero and unchanged. Internal compare does not assert while gated. Actual FROM_CPU3 IRQ is both enabled and pending but cannot execute the ISR or advance CPU1 instructions until release; afterwards the guest ISR acknowledges the real source. Timer ISR follows remaining counter ticks after release.
execution_contract.runstall: Clock remains positive, CPU1 instructions and ISR stop, but CCOUNT advances and internal timer becomes pending. ISR is delivered after release.
execution_contract.reset: RESETING increments only CPU1 local reset count. CPU0 guest counter/instruction loop continues; peripheral clock/enables, RTC marker and shared handshake survive.
execution_contract.scope: No physical hardware, encryption, executable injection, synthetic guest counter, mocks, LD_PRELOAD, frequency aliases, PC special cases, or timeout increases. Watchdogs are disabled because both fixture cores deliberately run private native spin loops.
